title: Deployment safeguard matrix: environment-aware canary/A-B/shadow orchestration
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design and implement a deployment safeguard matrix that encodes environment-specific constraints and safe defaults for canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and auto-rollback across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The goal is to provide a single policy surface that enforces config parity where possible, but also validates and synthesizes environment-specific overrides (eg. restricted network egress in Private, limited burst capacity in Dedicated).
motivation: Customers run identical model versions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but operational constraints differ. We need deterministic, auditable safeguards to prevent unsafe rollouts (eg. canaries that violate Private network policies or A/B splits that exceed committed Dedicated throughput). This reduces incidents and supports automated rollback with clear audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema that models environment capability flags, resource constraints, and permitted rollout primitives
Server-side admission checks that reject rollout requests violating Private/Dedicated constraints with actionable error messages
Rollout controller uses policy to synthesize safe canary parameters (initial weight, ramp cadence, max concurrent canaries) per environment
A/B and shadow rules validated to prevent exceeding Dedicated committed QPS and enforce data residency options for Private
Auto-rollback triggers (latency/error/slo regressions) plumbed through a single audit log entry with root cause markers
End-to-end e2e tests covering Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private promotion with a simulated constrained Dedicated pool and an isolated Private VPC
technical_notes: Policy schema: YAML-first with JSON Schema validation; fields: environment_capabilities, max_weight, ramp_schedule_templates, allowed_shadow_modes, required_kms_profile
Admission controller: run as webhook in control plane for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private control plane deploy a lightweight policy-checker binary with local policy bundle subscription
Rollout controller changes: policy-aware planner that transforms requested rollout into effective plan; planners run in runtime-1.22 agent
Auto-rollback: reuse existing SLO-eval pipeline (metrics + perf baselines) but add decision throttling and cooldown windows to avoid flapping
Compatibility: backward-compatible default policy for existing rollouts; opt-in enforcement flag per org for stricter checks
Observability: add policy_decision and effective_plan fields to rollout traces and console UI
design_decisions: Prefer declarative policy with environment capabilities rather than imperative per-environment code. Easier to extend for future on-prem constraints.
Admission vs runtime: reject obviously invalid requests at admission time; otherwise allow rollout and enforce guardrails dynamically to avoid blocking legitimate edge cases.
Shadow traffic handling: allow 'metric-only' shadowing in Private (no egress) while disallowing upstream-only shadows that would leak telemetry out of Private VPC.
Rollback aggressiveness: default to conservative thresholds in Private and Dedicated (lower latency tolerance) and a slightly more permissive stance in Hosted where we can auto-scale.
Storage of audit trails: use encrypted append-only log and expose user-facing rollback rationale in the Console with redaction for sensitive fields.

open_questions: How strict should defaults be for existing orgs? (opt-in strict enforcement vs gradual migration)
Should Dedicated enforcement include throttling tokens that decrement from committed pool or simply reject requests that exceed commit?
What is the authoritative source for Private environment capability flags — customer-supplied manifest or our installer-provisioned bundle?
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Nguyen): prefer clearer failure UX for owners when admission rejects a rollout — include remediation steps and estimated cost impact
Design (Lina Park): Console needs a compact policy diff view when promoting from Hosted -> Private so operators can quickly see required changes
Security (Rafael Gómez): mandate KMS-profile on any rollout that enables shadow traffic with telemetry export; also require audit log retention policy for Private customers
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize policy schema and admission error model; ship schema v0.1 and test vectors
Week 2: Implement admission webhook for Hosted + Dedicated; policy-bundle subscription mechanism for Private agent
Week 3: Integrate policy-aware rollout planner and add metric hooks for auto-rollback decisioning
Week 4: End-to-end test matrix across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, UX polish, and docs
Canary: enable opt-in per-org; gradual enablement with telemetry gating and safety net for rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): enable for Redwood infra org only with simulated Private VPC
Phase 1 (early customers): opt-in for Beta orgs; collect telemetry and iterate
Phase 2 (wider): default enforcement for new orgs; migration guide for existing orgs
Phase 3 (GA): enforcement on by default with audit logs and SSO-required approvals for sensitive rollouts
test_plan: Unit tests for policy schema validation and admission error messages
Integration tests: Hosted admission + rollout planner + auto-rollback using local metrics emulator
System tests: Dedicated capacity enforcement with simulated shared pool and contention scenarios
Private e2e: deploy policy-checker in isolated environment and validate no telemetry egress when telemetry_mode=private-only
Chaos test: introduce transient errors to ensure rollback cooldown prevents flapping
risks: Too-strict defaults could block customers' existing CI workflows — need migration path
Policy divergence between Hosted and Private if capability flags drift; requires clear sync path
Performance impact of admission checks on high-frequency rollout APIs — measured and mitigated with caching
Auto-rollback false positives if baselines are stale — need robust baseline refresh policy
